audit_findings.title: Possible double counting of equity-method joint ventures
audit_findings.magnitude: $61.793m of 2025 equity-method income and $335.690m of separately added stakes; actual overlap unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method income may enter the OE anchor while the underlying investments also enter the equity bridge as stakes.
audit_findings.evidence: Rather, we earn income (loss) from the equity method investment, which is inclusive of our proportionate share of net income (loss) of the joint venture for each period.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that equity-method income was $61.793m in 2025, equal to 38.1% of the $162.2m anchor, while $335.690m of stakes, equal to 12.8% of base equity value, is added separately. It does not establish whether the OE calculation removed that income and related distributions. If it did not, the same joint-venture economics are capitalized twice, readily changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year from filed net income and cash flow, explicitly removing equity-method income and distributions before adding stakes; obtain investee balance sheets to verify the $335.690m represents equity value net of joint-venture debt and senior claims.

audit_findings.title: Operating sales-type lease income may have been purged or capitalized incorrectly
audit_findings.magnitude: $112.456m of 2025 sales-type lease interest income; $608.264m of undiscounted future receipts, $402.243m of imputed interest and a $206.021m lease receivable
audit_findings.mechanism: Classification affects OE and growth: purging operating lease consideration understates OE, while perpetually capitalizing the accounting interest yield overstates OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest income increased by $64.7 million, or 135.4%, in the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily driven by income from certain of our commercial agreements with Delek Holdings that met the criteria to be accounted for as sales-type leases during the third quarter of 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: Sales-type lease interest was operating consideration from logistics agreements and equaled 69.3% of the $162.2m anchor. The finite receipt schedule and amortizing receivable also show that the accounting yield is not a perpetual operating stream. The record does not disclose exactly how the OE series treated interest, principal receipts, variable payments and residual value, so an error is not yet demonstrated, but either misapplication is plainly capable of changing value materially.
audit_findings.action: Trace every sales-type lease cash receipt into OE by year, separating interest, principal, variable payments and residual value from true portfolio interest; rerun the DCF using the contractual receipt schedule and only evidence-supported renewable operating economics thereafter.

audit_findings.title: Known post-2025 perimeter changes conflict with a null perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $110.0m gross sale consideration ($25.0m rail, $19.0m Tyler tank and $66.0m El Dorado terminal), 359,372 units returned, and $13.4m of first-half 2026 revenue lost from the East Texas marketing termination
audit_findings.mechanism: The changes affect normalized OE, the cash/stakes bridge and the fully diluted unit denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to these agreements, the Partnership agreed to sell a Tyler refinery tank to Delek Holdings for total consideration of $19.0 million (the “Tyler Tank Sale”) and to sell El Dorado tank and terminal assets to Delek Holdings for total consideration of $66.0 million (the “El Dorado Terminal Sale”).
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter-control error: the valuation records a null perimeter despite completed, contracted and pending changes known by the valuation date. The $110.0m gross consideration is 4.2% of base equity value, while the terminated marketing agreement reduced first-half 2026 revenue by $13.4m, 8.3% of the OE anchor, although revenue is not itself OE. The Tyler consideration also removed 359,372 outstanding units. These items cannot simply be netted because their timing, lost OE and retained obligations differ.
audit_findings.action: Build and rerun a dated perimeter bridge covering the East Texas termination, January 2026 El Dorado rail sale, April 2026 Tyler sale and pending October 2027 El Dorado terminal sale; reconcile asset-level lost OE, sale proceeds, debt or retained obligations, sales-type lease modifications and returned units to the latest balance sheet and denominator.

audit_findings.title: The fully diluted denominator may omit most outstanding phantom units
audit_findings.magnitude: 1,912,207 phantom units, equal to 3.59% of the 53.278996m denominator; full unit settlement would reduce base value from $49.32 to approximately $47.62 per unit
audit_findings.mechanism: Expected unit settlement increases the fully diluted denominator; cash settlement instead consumes equity value or future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: No Awards (as defined under the LTIP) have been made other than the phantom units, each of which represent rights to receive (upon vesting and payout) one common unit in the Partnership or an amount of cash equal to the fair market value of such unit.
audit_findings.explanation: The settlement mix remains unresolved, but the filed award count supplies a usable ceiling. Treating all 1,912,207 awards as incremental units would lower per-unit values by about 3.47%: bear from $42.77 to about $41.29, base from $49.32 to about $47.62 and bull from $54.32 to about $52.44. All remain below the $55.70 market price, and the margin-of-safety threshold would move only about $1.19 from $34.52 to approximately $33.33. Thus even the conservative ceiling does not reverse the stated valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile outstanding awards as of the valuation date by vesting probability, forfeiture, tax withholding and expected cash-versus-unit settlement, then replace the EPS-based increment with expected issuance or the equivalent cash claim.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital may be below the post-acquisition run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $29.192m annual difference between the $45.0m 2026 forecast and $15.808m deducted in 2025; if permanent and applied dollar-for-dollar to the anchor, approximately $410m or $7.70 per unit of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher normalized regulatory and sustaining capital reduces OE and therefore both forecast-period cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Regulatory and sustaining capital expenditures represent cash expenditures (including for the addition or improvement to, or the replacement of, our capital assets, and for the acquisition of existing, or the construction or development of new, capital assets) made to maintain our long-term operating income or operating capacity.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed 2026 forecast totals $45.0m of regulatory and sustaining capital, 2.85 times the 2025 deduction and 18.0% of the $162.2m anchor above the 2025 amount. With the valuation's fixed growth and discount assumptions, a permanent $29.192m anchor reduction would proportionately reduce the $2.279bn base operating PV by about $410m. The record does not establish whether the increase is temporary, but the filed scale is clearly capable of changing value materially.
audit_findings.action: Obtain asset-level 2025 actuals and 2026 forecast-to-actual spending for Gravity, H2O, gas processing and legacy assets; classify recurring sustaining requirements, including capitalized internal labor and interest, and rerun every OE year and the anchor using a normalized maintenance schedule.

audit_findings.title: Environmental and retirement claims are absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.157m filed asset-retirement obligation at June 30, 2026; other environmental obligations unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unreserved or unnormalized remediation and retirement cash costs reduce OE or require a separate senior-claim deduction from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We also have other non-current liabilities pertaining to environmental liabilities and asset retirement obligations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed ARO equals about 1.0% of the $2.628bn base equity value, or approximately $0.49 per unit if deducted in full, so that identified balance alone is not material to the conclusion. However, environmental obligations are not separately quantified, and the record does not establish whether OE contains an adequate normalized cash reserve, whether accretion already captures part of the burden, or how much is recoverable from insurance or Delek. Materiality of the remaining exposure therefore cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest ARO and environmental-liability schedules, expected settlement cash flows, discounting, insurance coverage and Delek indemnification; reconcile amounts already charged through OE and deduct only the uncovered present value not otherwise captured.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.575m FY2024 residual, computed as $96.375m filed D&A less $76.8m identified; eligible recurring portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be non-economic and eligible would be added back to OE, increasing the historical series and potentially the trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2024 $76.8m (79.7% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: Leaving the residual as an expense is conservative and cannot overstate value, but it may understate OE. The FY2024 residual is 12.1% of the $162.2m anchor; if the entire amount were recurring, eligible and added dollar-for-dollar to the anchor, base operating value would rise by roughly $275m or $5.16 per unit. The record provides no classification across the full OE series, so neither eligibility nor actual anchor impact is demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the fixed-asset and intangible-amortization rollforwards underlying residual D&A for every OE year; identify only non-economic components not already offset by maintenance capital, then rerun the OE series and trend anchor for the supported portion.
